R0109.title: Broken Authorization Risk
R0109.definition: An authenticated user or process accesses resources, data objects, or administrative interfaces beyond its assigned role, tenant, object, or operation permissions, or performs unauthorized business functions, administrative actions, or cross-tenant operations because post-authentication authorization checks fail. Typical forms include horizontal privilege escalation, vertical privilege escalation, missing object-level authorization, and server-side permission checks bypassed through parameter tampering.
R0109.description:
Broken authorization occurs after a principal has logged in or otherwise authenticated, but the application fails to verify permission for the requested object or action. Attackers may tamper with user, order, or tenant identifiers to read peer users' data, causing horizontal privilege escalation, or invoke administrative endpoints and alter role parameters to gain higher privileges, causing vertical privilege escalation.

The defining condition is authenticated access without correct authorization. It differs from R0293, where effective authentication is absent or the target interface has no authentication control. Servers must enforce authorization for every request and resource rather than relying on hidden UI elements, unpredictable identifiers, or login state alone.
R0109.influence: Broken authorization can expose cross-user or cross-tenant data, let low-privilege accounts perform administrative actions, enable business-data tampering, and amplify losses from stolen accounts.

references.title: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key
